title: Glasshouse — institutional accountability evidence dataset (say vs. do)
description:
Glasshouse is a public, machine-readable record of what large asset managers say about how they vote their funds' shares (archived proxy-voting and stewardship policies, with dates) and how those funds actually voted (SEC Form N-PX), with 13-F holdings and a public enforcement record alongside.

This version holds 20,022,329 fund vote lines from meetings between 1 July 2023 and 30 June 2026, filed by fund trusts of 28 financial institutions. For 25 of them (BlackRock, Dimensional, Vanguard, State Street, Fidelity, American Century, Nuveen/TIAA, Capital Group, Columbia Threadneedle, Northern Trust, MFS, Morgan Stanley, AllianceBernstein, Wellington, Federated Hermes, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Parametric, Janus Henderson, Invesco, Charles Schwab, DWS, T. Rowe Price, BNY, Franklin Templeton) every kind of vote is on file for the fund trusts held; for UBS, BNP Paribas and Bank of America only executive-pay (say-on-pay) votes are on file. The fund trusts held are often a small part of a large manager: this is not a complete record of any manager's voting. Some 2025–2026 Dimensional N-PX exhibits contain exactly 500,000 proxy records in the SEC file itself and appear capped, so their counts are lower bounds. It also holds 163 dated versions of 26 managers' policy documents (hashes, dates and archive links; no policy text), 580,106 13-F holding rows and 14,887 enforcement actions.

Correction. Versions 2026-11-17.2, 2026-11-17.3, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-18.2 shipped repeated N-PX vote lines as distinct votes (0.62–0.69% of their votes; mostly Dimensional, whose line counts there are about 3% too high). This version is corrected: no shipped vote is a marked duplicate, and the build now refuses to run when duplicate flags are stale. Per-release counts: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not/blob/main/docs/CORRECTIONS.md

New in this version: Morgan Stanley Investment Management, MFS, American Century, Janus Henderson, AllianceBernstein and Federated Hermes fund registrants, each keyed to its voting adviser from the funds' own SAIs, with dated policy text (website captures and copies printed in fund SAIs); Parametric's 2026 votes are paired with the Morgan Stanley policy its funds' SAIs print. A policy version's identity is now computed from the policy text only (web-page menus and trademark spacing are ignored) and shipped as identity_sha256, so a restored copy reproduces the same version counts.

Votes are attributed to the adviser that cast them, not the brand: where one group's funds are voted by different advisers under different policies every vote carries an adviser_key, and a policy may only be compared with votes of the same key. Three derived tables give one row per manager per ballot item (shareholder proposals, director elections, say-on-pay). Every column and code is defined in DATASHEET.md; coverage and known gaps are stated in COVERAGE.json; every file is checksummed in MANIFEST.sha256.

Code: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not (MIT). The DATASHEET records the exact code commit that built these files.

The dataset records facts from public filings. It makes no finding of wrongdoing about anyone.
notes: Code: MIT. Data: CC-BY-4.0. Built from code commit recorded in DATASHEET.md.
